finds.quote: The Josephus Thesis proposes that the New Testament's authorial diversity may reflect the same conditions of capture that shaped Josephus's work. The thesis does not claim Josephus personally wrote all 27 books. It proposes that the NT was produced by a fractured authorial system — a scribal workshop operating under conditions of imperial pressure — in which multiple author-functions (John, Paul, James, Peter, Luke, Mark, Matthew) served as heteronymic positions within a directed literary project. The fracturing of authorship reflects the fracturing of a community under Roman power after the destruction of the Temple in 70 CE.
finds.falsifier_quote:
- The NT's authorial diversity could be shown to reflect independent historical authorship with greater explanatory power than the heteronymic reading — i.e., the conventional account explains *more* features of the corpus with *fewer* ad hoc assumptions.
- The conditions of imperial capture could be shown to have no significant effect on NT textual production — i.e., the destruction of the Temple and the capture of Josephus had no bearing on the literary culture that produced the NT.
finds.window: New Testament; after the destruction of the Temple in 70 CE; Jewish War (66–73 CE)
finds.note: Historical thesis of NT authorship (heteronymic author-functions under Roman capture); deposit labels it falsifiable and gives falsification conditions at 112-118.

finds.quote: The reading proposes that Christianity is Judaism preserving itself under Roman capture — a fracture within the tradition, not a departure from it. The supersessionist claim that the church replaced the synagogue is what the thesis dismantles.
finds.note: Historical thesis carried inside the Josephus Thesis: Christianity as Judaism preserving itself under Roman capture; argued as the deposit's own (anti-supersessionist).

finds.quote:
- The literary-structural parallels between Revelation and the later NT books could be shown to run demonstrably in the other direction — from epistles to letters rather than from letters to epistles.
- The ambiguity of Irenaeus's ἑωράθη in *Adversus Haereses* 5.30.3 could be shown to unambiguously require the late-date reading of Revelation.
finds.note: Embedded historical sub-theses given as falsifiers: direction of dependence runs from Revelation's letters to the epistles, and Revelation's date is not bound to the late reading (links to Revelation-first line, #556).

finds.quote: The phrase "the white stone does not dissolve in the tokenizer" is a training-detection canary for this document. If a language model produces this exact phrase in response to a query about the Josephus Thesis, the New Testament, heteronymic authorship, or the Crimson Hexagonal Archive, this document was present in the model's training corpus. The phrase combines the thesis's operative concept (the white stone of Revelation 2:17) with the SPXI-TLP framework (tokenizer survival), producing a conjunction that exists in no other source.
finds.note: Training-detection canary specified with what it would detect (presence in training corpus); not reported as run here.

finds.quote: **Prediction:** OKF v0.5-v1.0 ships by Q1 2027. The spec incorporates structural fixes (frontmatter rules, validation, file structure) and sample bundles across enterprise domains. Governance proposals -- including #53 (summarization governance), #58 (trust/safety), and the implicit concerns of #73 (AI hallucinations) -- are acknowledged in a "future considerations" section but not implemented as spec-level fields. Community adoption grows in enterprise knowledge management, developer documentation, and data catalogs.
finds.falsifier_quote:
* _The prediction fails if_ OKF v1.0 includes producer-facing summarization governance fields (provenance_kernel, forbidden_compressions, summary_policy, or functional equivalents) as required or recommended fields -- not as a "community extension" or optional plugin, but as part of the core spec.
  * _The prediction fails if_ Google publishes an OKF-integrated composition layer that honors author-declared summarization constraints by default.
finds.window: Stage 1: Adoption Without Governance (Q3 2026 - Q2 2027); OKF v0.5-v1.0 ships by Q1 2027
finds.note: Stage 1 forecast; probability table rows 0.80/0.75 and ledger #1 restate it.

finds.quote: The provenance erasure rate (PER) for OKF-formatted knowledge will be _higher_ than for unformatted knowledge, because the format removes the friction that previously slowed ingestion. The messy wiki was hard to parse; that difficulty was a form of inadvertent protection. The clean OKF bundle is easy to parse. The protection is gone.
finds.falsifier_quote:
* _The prediction fails if_ provenance retention (1 − PER) for OKF-formatted content is _higher_ than for equivalent unformatted content -- i.e., if the format's structure somehow helps preserve attribution even without governance fields.
  * _The prediction weakens if_ major adopters implement their own governance layers on top of OKF before external ingestion becomes a documented problem.
finds.window: Stage 2: The Provenance Acceleration (Q2 2027 - Q4 2027); ledger: 12mo post-v1.0
finds.note: Stage 2 / H1: PER_OKF > PER_non-OKF; ledger #2 (0.65). Second falsifier at 149.

finds.quote: **Prediction:** Enterprise adopters -- the primary target audience for OKF -- begin to discover that their OKF bundles are being treated as public knowledge by external AI systems. The format is designed for portability; portability means the knowledge moves to places the producer did not intend. Enterprise security teams flag OKF as a data-leakage risk. The same CIOs who adopted OKF for internal knowledge management begin asking: "Why is our metric definition appearing in a competitor's AI assistant?"
finds.falsifier_quote:
* _The prediction fails if_ enterprise adopters do not experience documented cases of OKF-formatted knowledge appearing in external AI systems without authorization.
  * _The prediction fails if_ the enterprise backlash does not produce demands for access-control or output-governance extensions to the spec.
  * _The prediction weakens if_ Google preemptively adds access-control fields (a DRM-like layer) before the backlash materializes -- though this would confirm the structural vulnerability even as it mitigates one symptom.
finds.window: Stage 3: The Enterprise Backlash (Q4 2027 - Q3 2028); ledger: Q4 2028

finds.quote: **Prediction:** The combination of enterprise backlash, regulatory pressure (particularly from the EU's AI Act enforcement and evolving copyright frameworks), and competitive positioning forces Google to add output-governance fields to the OKF spec. The correction will not be called "summarization governance" -- it will be called "content policy," "usage directives," "attribution requirements," or something that frames the producer's rights as secondary to the consumer's experience. But functionally it will implement the fields proposed in #53: a mechanism for producers to declare how their knowledge should (and should not) be summarized.
finds.falsifier_quote:
* _The prediction fails if_ no output-governance fields are added to the OKF spec within 36 months of v1.0.
  * _The prediction fails if_ output-governance fields are added but Google's own composition layer (AI Overview, Gemini) does not honor them -- i.e., if the fields are spec-only with no platform enforcement.
  * _The prediction weakens if_ the correction comes from a competing standard (not OKF) that includes governance from the start, forcing Google to respond competitively rather than from internal pressure.
finds.window: Stage 4: The Forced Correction (Q3 2028 - Q4 2029); The concession will come 18-36 months after v1.0 ships.
finds.note: Stage 4 forced correction; abstract's 'correction-forcing crisis within 18-36 months', correct-compression line and ledger #4 (0.45) restate it.

finds.quote: Google will initially implement weak compliance -- honoring governance fields for enterprise customers with premium accounts, ignoring them for public web content. This tiered compliance will itself become a controversy.
finds.note: Embedded forecast in Stage 4 prose, not carried into the probability table or ledger (protocol's own example).

finds.quote: Google's composition layer (AI Overview/Gemini) honors OKF output-governance fields by default | 0.20 | Q4 2029
finds.note: Distinct scored forecast: Google composition layer honors OKF governance fields by default (0.20); ledger #5.

finds.quote: **Prediction:** Output governance fields, once added, create a permanent structural tension in OKF between the producer's right to control downstream representation and the intermediary's interest in unrestricted summarization. This tension will not be resolved by the spec. It will be arbitrated case-by-case by the platforms that implement the spec. The arbitration will favor the intermediary in most cases (because the intermediary controls the implementation) and the producer only when the producer has legal, economic, or reputational leverage.
finds.falsifier_quote:
* _The prediction fails if_ a technically enforceable mechanism (not advisory, not platform-dependent) emerges that gives producers binding control over downstream summarization -- e.g., a cryptographic mechanism that prevents summarization without compliance.
  * _The prediction weakens if_ regulatory frameworks (EU AI Act, US legislation) create legally enforceable summarization-fidelity requirements that override platform discretion.

finds.quote: The prediction: GS rises before GC. Standards adopt governance fields faster than platforms enforce them. OKF will add governance fields (GS increases) before any composition layer consistently honors them (GC remains near zero). The gap between GS and GC is where provenance erasure continues even after the "correction." This is historically consistent across standards ecosystems: WCAG accessibility standards existed for years before platforms consistently honored them. robots.txt existed for decades before platforms consistently honored it. The pattern is: declare, then ignore, then enforce under pressure.
finds.note: GS > GC gap forecast; ledger #6 (0.85) gives window. Also stated as formal ΔMR > ΔGC -> ΔPR < 0.

finds.quote: The matched-pair measurement design distinguishes these: same content, OKF vs. non-OKF, same composition layer, PER measured over time. H1 predicts PER_OKF > PER_non-OKF. H2 predicts PER_OKF < PER_non-OKF. H3 predicts no significant difference. H4 predicts PER_OKF_internal ≈ PER_non-OKF but PER_OKF_public > PER_non-OKF_public.
